edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Moderate exercise may be the sweet spot where mood benefit is substantial but dropout and overtraining are less likely than at very high doses.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2026 Zeng meta analysis in Psychooncology, which suggests that moderate-dose exercise tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for depression. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
